texts.li: A board propped by the gate says, in careful chalk, "Letters written and read. Fair hand, fair price." It belongs to {X_nameDef}, a scribe of {FACTION}, who has set up at the colony's table with quills, ink and a stack of good paper.\n\nFor {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will write a letter for anyone who wants one, to anywhere a road goes, and see it carried by the next rider. {A_nameDef} has already started thinking about who to write to.

A scribe of {FACTION} named {X_nameDef} has come up the road with a writing desk strapped on like a peddler's pack. Most folk can't read or write, {X_nameDef} says, and most folk have someone they'd like to tell something to. For {COUNT} silver, anyone here can send word home.

[winter] {X_nameDef}, a scribe of {FACTION}, came in out of the snow with the ink frozen in its pot and asked to sit by the hearth until it thawed. In return, for {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} offers to write the colony's letters, one for anyone who wants to send word somewhere.

[colony:Traditional] Word on the road is that the colony keeps its customs and its records. So {X_nameDef}, a scribe of {FACTION}, has come to offer a fair copy of the colony's own story, or letters home for anyone who wants them, for {COUNT} silver.

[trait:TooSmart] {X_nameDef}, a traveling scribe of {FACTION}, has set up at the colony's table. {A_nameDef} has already read everything {X_nameDef} brought and corrected two of the spellings. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will still write the colony's letters.

li.label: Letters for anyone who wants one ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} wrote until the candle burned down: letters to mothers, to old friends, to a creditor or two. They'll go out with the next rider bound that way.

outcomes.li: [winter] {X_nameDef} wrote by the fire all evening, letter after letter, blowing on the ink to dry it. They'll go out with the first rider after the thaw.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} went last, and asked {X_nameDef} to write to the family of someone {A_pronoun} once knew, to say they were remembered.

li.label: A fair copy of the colony's story (half that)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spent the evening telling the colony's story from the beginning, and {X_nameDef} wrote it down in a fair round hand. The copy is bound in leather and kept on the shelf now.

outcomes.li: [colony:Traditional] {X_nameDef} wrote the colony's story out fair, with the names of the dead in red ink. It sits on the shelf by the hearth, open at the first page.

li.label: the telling of the colony's story
Have {X_objective} teach reading to anyone who'll sit still (half that)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sat the colony down round the table with chalk and a board, and by the end of the evening most of them could write their own names, and a few could read someone else's.

li.label: No letters today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} packs away the quills, sleeps the night, and goes on to the next village.

texts.li: [industrial] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came up the road with a wooden tripod over one shoulder and a camera the size of a bread box. Pictures of settlements are how {X_nameDef} makes a living, and the colony is the first place in weeks where anyone looks willing to stand still.\n\nFor {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will take a picture of everyone at the colony and leave a print to hang on the wall.

[spacer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} travels the rim taking pictures on film, on purpose, because files get lost and paper lasts. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will take one of all of them together and leave a print, a real one, the kind that fades slowly in a frame.

There's a tripod by the gate, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} behind it, squinting at the colony through the lens. {X_nameDef} would like to take its picture, the whole lot of it out front and standing still, for {COUNT} silver and a print to keep.

[children] {X_nameDef}, a photographer of {FACTION}, is having a hard time with the colony's children, who want to look through the camera, touch the camera and stand in front of the camera at the same time. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will take a picture of the colony, if it can be made to stand still.

[colony:Hardworking] People at work are what {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} likes to photograph, and word is the colony never stops working. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will take one of the whole lot of them out front, tools in hand.

li.label: Everyone out front ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: It took the better part of an hour to get the whole lot of them still at the same moment, and {A_nameDef} blinked anyway. The print is drying on the kitchen wall.

outcomes.li: [children] The children wouldn't stand still, so they're a blur across the front of the picture. It's the part people look at first.
[colony:Hardworking] The colony stood for the picture in its work clothes, tools in hand, because none of them would take the time to change. The print hangs in the workshop now.
[trait:Ugly] {A_nameDef} stood at the very back, half behind someone else. It's still a good picture.

li.label: Let {X_objective} take pictures for {FACTION}'s papers
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} spent the day photographing the colony at work, and paid half of {COUNT} silver for the right to print the best of them in {FACTION}'s papers.
li.riskOutcome: The picture that ran in {FACTION}'s paper was of the latrine, from an unfortunate angle, with {A_nameDef} coming out of it. At least the silver was paid.

li.label: No pictures
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} folds up the tripod with a sigh and goes looking for a more photogenic settlement.

outcomes.li: [colony:Guarded] The colony would rather not be in anyone's papers. {X_nameDef} packs up and goes.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has come a very long way to be uncomfortable. A traveler from a glitterworld, by way of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef} paid a guide to bring {X_objective} to a real rim colony, and would like to stay two days and live as the colonists live.\n\n{X_nameDef} will pay {COUNT} silver for it, and has brought four cases of luggage.

[spacer] A shuttle from {FACTION} set down beyond the hills, and {X_nameDef} walked the rest of the way in a sun hat, with a camera and a guide to the rim that has the colony's region circled. {X_nameDef} would like to stay two days and experience real frontier life, and will pay {COUNT} silver to do it.

[industrial] {X_nameDef}, a wealthy traveler from somewhere much nicer, arrived in the company of {FACTION}'s traders with a hired guide and a crate of bottled water. {X_nameDef} wants to spend two days living the rim life at the colony, and offers {COUNT} silver for the privilege.

[summer] {X_nameDef}, a tourist from a glitterworld traveling with {FACTION}, has already been bitten by something and is delighted about it. {X_nameDef} would like to stay two days at the colony and do whatever the colonists do, and will pay {COUNT} silver.

[winter] {X_nameDef} has come from a glitterworld where the weather is decided by committee, and has never seen snow fall on its own. {X_nameDef} would like to stay two days at the colony, cold and all, and will pay {COUNT} silver for it.

li.label: Take {X_objective} as a paying guest ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} pays in full up front, unpacks a great deal of luggage, and within the hour has asked {A_nameDef} three times where the water comes from. It's the most authentic thing {X_pronoun} has ever done, {X_nameDef} says.

outcomes.li: [winter] Within the hour of paying, {X_nameDef} is lying in the yard making a snow angel, which {X_pronoun} then photographs from every side.
[trait:Greedy] Before the luggage is even unpacked, {A_nameDef} has sold {X_nameDef} a carved spoon for twice what it's worth.

li.label: Put {X_objective} to work, as promised
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} put {X_nameDef} on the barn, the woodpile and the latrine, in that order. {X_nameDef} hated every minute, said so, and paid extra on the way out for the stories it would make.

outcomes.li: [b:trait:Kind] {B_nameDef} found {X_nameDef} the easiest of the hard jobs and kept {X_objective} company while doing them. {X_nameDef} left tired, filthy and happy, and paid extra.

li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} lasted until lunch on the first day, sat down in the barn and asked for a refund. {B_nameDef} talked {X_objective} down to half.

li.label: No guests, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is disappointed, takes a few pictures of the gate, and leaves with the guide.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked into the colony with a drum on {X_possessive} back and bells braided into {X_possessive} hair. A spirit-singer, {A_nameDef} says: one who goes from camp to camp singing to the spirits of the land, so they stay friendly to the people living on it.\n\n{X_nameDef} would sing for the colony tonight, for a meal and a place at the fire.

[grave] A spirit-singer of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, came to the colony at dusk and went straight to the graves, and stood among them a long while before saying a word. When {X_nameDef} did speak, it was to {A_nameDef}: the colony's dead are restless, and would sleep better for a song.

[winter] {X_nameDef}, a spirit-singer of {FACTION}, came out of the snow with frost in {X_possessive} hair and a drum wrapped in hide against the cold. Winter is when the spirits are hungriest, {X_nameDef} says, and offers to sing to them tonight on the colony's behalf, for a bowl of something hot.

[colony:Traditional] "This land has not been sung to in a long time. I can hear it." {X_nameDef}, a spirit-singer of {FACTION}, has walked a long way because word reached {X_possessive} people of a colony that keeps the old ways. {X_nameDef} would sing at its fire tonight, for food and a place to sleep.

[river] {X_nameDef}, a spirit-singer of {FACTION}, has come up from the river with wet feet and a drum. The river spirit is old and easily offended, {X_nameDef} says, and has been neglected here. {X_nameDef} would sing to it tonight, and to the land, for a meal.

li.label: Let {X_objective} sing to the land (10 food)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sang until the fire burned down, low and steady, one long song with the drum under it like a heartbeat. In the morning the spirit-singer was gone, and the bowl was licked clean.

outcomes.li: [winter] {X_nameDef} sang to the winter spirits through the coldest part of the night, and the colony sat close round the fire to listen.

[river] {X_nameDef} sang down at the riverbank in the dark, with the colonists standing on the bank behind. In the morning the water looked no different, but more than one of them stopped on the way past to look at it.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to sing for our dead (10 food)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} went from grave to grave in the dusk, singing each one a short song of its own. The colony stood back and listened, and some of them cried.

outcomes.li: [trait:Psychopath] {X_nameDef} sang at every grave in turn. {A_nameDef} watched the others more than the singer.

li.label: Feed {X_objective} and send {X_objective} on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} eats, thanks the colony, and walks on in the morning to sing for someone else.

li.reason: There are no graves here to sing over.

texts.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a roll of knives and a sack of spices none of the colonists can name. Cooking for whoever will feed {X_objective} is how {X_nameDef} gets by on the road, and {X_nameDef} has an offer: the run of the kitchen and the stores for a day, and the colony will eat better tonight than it has all year.\n\nOr, for {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will teach whoever cooks here a few things they don't know.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a cook of {FACTION} who gave up a restaurant kitchen for the road, wants a day in the colony's kitchen. Give {X_nameDef} the stores and a free hand, and the colony will remember the meal.\n\nOr, for {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will spend the day teaching the colony's own cook.

[colony:Thrifty] A traveling cook of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, took one look in the colony's stores and laughed: all those good things, and the same stew on the table every night. {X_nameDef} offers to show the colony what its stores can do, or to teach its cook for {COUNT} silver.

[trait:Gourmand] {A_nameDef} has been hovering by the kitchen door since {X_nameDef}, a traveling cook of {FACTION}, put down {X_possessive} bags, and has already asked what's for supper. {X_nameDef} would cook a feast from the colony's stores tonight, or teach the colony's cook for {COUNT} silver.

[fall] The stores are full, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, who cooks harvest feasts for whoever will have {X_objective}, says it would be a crime not to do something with them. It's the right time of year for it.

li.label: Give {X_objective} the kitchen (40 food)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} took over the kitchen for the day with {B_nameDef} chopping and fetching, and the colony ate a supper it will still be talking about next season.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef} dug a pit, lined it with hot stones and buried half the stores in it, and at sundown dug it all back up again, cooked. {B_nameDef} wrote nothing down and remembers all of it.
[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} used every pot in the kitchen and a few things that aren't pots. {B_nameDef} washed up for three hours afterwards and says it was worth it.
[fall] {X_nameDef} made a harvest supper of seven dishes, with {B_nameDef} running between the pots, and the colony ate until it couldn't move.

li.label: Have {X_objective} teach our cook ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: All day {X_nameDef} stood at {B_nameDef}'s elbow, correcting how {B_nameDef} holds a knife, salts a pot and judges a fire. {B_nameDef} came out of it a better cook and very tired.

outcomes.li: [b:trait:Abrasive] {X_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about salt for most of the morning. By evening they had agreed on salt, and {B_nameDef} had learned a great deal.

li.label: Not today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs, eats what the colony eats, and leaves in the morning with polite things to say about it.

texts.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a bone-setter and herb-healer of {FACTION}, stopped at the gate on the way through, took one look at {A_nameDef} and asked how long the {TALE} had been bothering {A_objective}.\n\nFor {COUNT} silver, or a few doses of medicine to take on the road, {X_nameDef} would see to it today.

[industrial] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} travels the settlements with a doctor's bag and a tired horse, seeing to whatever the town doctors won't. {X_nameDef} spotted {A_nameDef}'s {TALE} from across the yard, and offers to treat it today, for {COUNT} silver or a few doses of medicine.

[spacer] {X_nameDef}, a traveling medic of {FACTION}, ran a hand scanner over {A_nameDef} without being asked, frowned at the readout, and pronounced it a {TALE}. {X_nameDef} can deal with that in an afternoon, for {COUNT} silver or a few doses of medicine for the road.

[ail:StrainedBack] {A_nameDef} bent for a bucket and straightened up again very slowly, and {X_nameDef}, a bone-setter of {FACTION} passing through, saw it from the gate. {X_nameDef} has hands like a blacksmith's and a name for fixing backs, and offers to put {A_nameDef}'s right, for {COUNT} silver or some medicine for the road.

[ail:Toothache] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} pulls teeth, among other things, and the swelling on {A_nameDef}'s jaw caught {X_possessive} eye straight away. For {COUNT} silver, or a few doses of medicine, {X_nameDef} will deal with it before supper.

[ail:SprainedAnkle] {X_nameDef}, a healer of {FACTION}, saw {A_nameDef} limping across the yard and was kneeling at {A_possessive} foot before {A_nameDef} could object. A proper strapping and a poultice would have it right in days, {X_nameDef} says, for {COUNT} silver or some medicine in trade.

[ail:HeadCold|ail:ChestCold] {X_nameDef}, an herb-healer of {FACTION}, heard {A_nameDef} coughing from the road and came in to see about it. {X_nameDef} has a tea for that, and a rub for the chest, and will leave {A_nameDef} with both for {COUNT} silver or a few doses of medicine.

[ail:Sunburn|ail:Blisters] One look at {A_nameDef}'s {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, who sells salves on the road, was already reaching into the bag. For {COUNT} silver, or some medicine in trade, {X_nameDef} will see to it properly.

li.label: Pay {X_objective} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: A poultice, a strong-smelling tea and a great deal of advice: {X_nameDef} gave {A_nameDef} the whole afternoon. {A_nameDef} already feels better, and has the advice written down somewhere.

outcomes.li: [ail:StrainedBack] {X_nameDef} laid {A_nameDef} face down on the table, found the knot with two thumbs and did something that made a noise like a branch snapping. {A_nameDef} stood up straight for the first time in days.
[ail:Toothache] {X_nameDef} took the tooth out in one pull while {A_nameDef} was still deciding whether to be brave. The swelling's going down already.
[spacer] {X_nameDef} gave {A_nameDef} an injection and a strip of pills, and told {A_objective} to stop being so hard on {A_objective}self. The first part is working.

li.label: Pay in medicine (2), and let our doctor watch
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} treated {A_nameDef} with {B_nameDef} watching every move and asking questions until {X_nameDef} ran out of answers. {A_nameDef} is on the mend, and {B_nameDef} has filled a page with notes.

outcomes.li: [b:office:Physician] The colony's physician, {B_nameDef}, watched {X_nameDef} work and argued with two of the three things {X_pronoun} did. The third was new, and {B_nameDef} wrote it down.

li.label: {A_nameDef} will mend on {A_possessive} own
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} leaves {A_nameDef} with some free advice and goes on down the road.

outcomes.li: [trait:Tough] {A_nameDef} says it's nothing, and sees {X_nameDef} off at the gate. It isn't nothing, but it'll pass.

texts.li: [medieval] {X_nameDef}, a wandering fiddler of {FACTION}, has stopped for the night. {X_nameDef} noticed {A_nameDef} across the yard, gray in the face and short with whoever speaks to {A_objective}, and has offered to play a tune for {A_objective} alone tonight. That, {X_nameDef} says, is what musicians are for.

[tribal] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} plays the bone flute, and came to the colony's fire at dusk to play for supper. {X_nameDef} hasn't taken {X_possessive} eyes off {A_nameDef}, who looks like {A_pronoun} hasn't slept in a week. Some songs are for a whole camp, {X_nameDef} says, and some are for one person.

[industrial|spacer] A battered guitar, a meal a night, one settlement after another: that's how {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} lives. Tonight {X_nameDef} has noticed {A_nameDef}, worn thin and snapping at whoever comes near, and has offered, without any fuss, to play just for {A_objective} after supper.

[worn|breaking] {A_nameDef} has been holding together by a thread for days. A traveling musician of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, sat beside {A_objective} at supper and didn't say much, and afterwards asked the council if {X_nameDef} could play for {A_nameDef} tonight, somewhere quiet.

After supper, if the council likes, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} will play. For {COUNT} silver it can be for the whole table. For nothing at all, it can be for {A_nameDef}, who looks like {A_pronoun} needs it most.

{X_nameDef}, a traveling musician of {FACTION}, has asked for a bed for the night and offered to play for it. {X_nameDef} has already picked out the face that needs a song most: {A_nameDef}'s, tired and gray. {X_nameDef} would play for {A_objective} alone, for nothing, or for everyone, for {COUNT} silver.

A singer of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, came in with the evening and sat by the door to listen to the colony before playing a note. {X_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} sounds like someone who needs a quiet song, and offers one.

li.label: Let {X_objective} play for {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} sat out by the woodpile after dark, and {X_nameDef} played slow tunes until {A_nameDef} fell asleep where {A_pronoun} sat. Someone fetched a blanket.

outcomes.li: [tribal] {X_nameDef} played the bone flute for {A_nameDef} alone, out past the firelight, until the stars wheeled round. {A_nameDef} came back to bed quiet and slept through till morning.
[trait:Abrasive] {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} to leave {A_objective} alone, twice. {X_nameDef} played anyway, and by the third song {A_nameDef} had stopped complaining.
[breaking] {X_nameDef} sat with {A_nameDef} half the night, playing and not talking. Near the end {A_nameDef} cried, and then slept.

li.label: A song for everyone after supper ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} played for the whole colony after supper: fast ones first, then slow ones, until the fire was low. {A_nameDef} sat near the front and sang along to one of them.

li.label: Thank {X_objective}, and let {X_objective} go on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} played two or three tunes at supper anyway, and was gone in the morning.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} and a few others of {FACTION} have come to the colony with an unusual request. Word has reached {PLACE} that the colony decides things in council, by talking it through and voting, and {FACTION} would like to see how that's done.\n\nThey ask to stay a day, talk to whoever will talk to them, and sit at the back if the council meets.

[theirLowtech] Among {FACTION}, the eldest decides and the rest listen. {X_nameDef}, who has come from {PLACE} with company, has heard that the colony does things differently, with a council where everyone has a say, and would like to see it for {X_objective}self.

[theirHightech] The request came ahead of them, typed and stamped: "Delegation from {PLACE} requests permission to observe the colony's council in session. Duration one day. No interference intended."\n\n{FACTION} are run by a board that hasn't met in person in years. {X_nameDef}, who signed the request, is at the gate now, with a notebook already open.

[colony:Open] A colony that's open with its neighbors, the talk in {PLACE} goes, might not mind being watched. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come from there with company to ask a favor: a seat at the back of the colony's council, to learn how it's done.

li.label: Let them watch, and ask what they like
li.outcome: The envoys from {FACTION} spent the day asking who decides what and why, and wrote down everything. They left at dawn, thoughtful.

outcomes.li: [theirLowtech] The envoys' eldest listened all day with folded arms, and at the end said only that it seemed a slow way to decide anything. The younger ones asked a great many questions on the road out.
[office:Speaker] {A_nameDef}, the colony's speaker, walked the envoys through how a question comes to the council and how it's settled. They left with pages of notes.

li.label: Feed them well and show them everything (20 food)
li.outcome: The envoys were shown the fields, the workshops and the council's table, and fed at the colony's own. They went home to {PLACE} with full stomachs and a lot to say.

li.label: The council's business is its own
li.outcome: The envoys are thanked and told no. They stay the night as guests and go home to {PLACE} in the morning.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a peacemaker of {FACTION}, settles quarrels for a living: between families, between villages, now and then between whole peoples. {X_nameDef} had been at the colony less than an hour before noticing {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} taking care not to look at each other across the yard.\n\n{X_nameDef} offers to sit the two of them down tonight and see what can be done.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} carries a peace-staff, which among {X_possessive} people means anyone at odds may ask for a hearing. {X_nameDef} has heard about {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} already, from three different people, and offers to hear them both out.

[!lowtech] Mediators notice things, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is a mediator. Within an hour of arriving, {X_nameDef} had asked {A_nameDef} what the trouble with {B_nameDef} was, and asked {B_nameDef} the same about {A_nameDef}.\n\nThe answers didn't match. {X_nameDef} would like to sit them down together.

[colony:Easygoing] {X_nameDef}, a peacemaker of {FACTION}, says the colony is a pleasant place with one sore spot in it, and the sore spot is {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} offers to do something about it before moving on.

"Those two," said {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} at supper, with a nod at {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}, who were eating at opposite ends of the table. "How long has that been going on?"\n\n{X_nameDef} has spent thirty years mending quarrels up and down the roads, and offers to sit the two of them down together before moving on.
A quiet traveler of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, says {X_pronoun} has settled worse feuds than the one between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}, and offers to try tonight, if the council agrees.

li.label: Let {X_objective} sit them down
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sat {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} down at the kitchen table with a pot of tea and didn't let either of them leave until well past midnight. They came out talking to each other, carefully, like people testing ice.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef} laid the peace-staff on the ground between them and made each of them say the other's side of it out loud. It took half the night. They walked back together.
[trait:Abrasive] It got loud for a while, mostly {A_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} waited it out, and by the end {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} had agreed on something, which {X_nameDef} says is how it starts.

li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} tried, and kept trying until the fire went out. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} left the table no friendlier than they sat down.

li.label: Set them a job to do together
li.outcome: On {X_nameDef}'s advice, the council set {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to rebuild the woodpile together. By evening they were arguing about the right way to stack logs, which {X_nameDef} says is progress.

li.label: Leave them to it
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is thanked and told the colony will sort its own quarrels. {X_nameDef} doesn't look convinced.
